Desktop Publishing · Week 9 · Title

Multi-page documents: the newsletter

A newsletter repeats a structure on every page: masthead, columns, styles, page numbers.

Next Generation Genius · Year 1 · Foundation

Desktop Publishing · Week 9 · Goals

By the end of today

  • Use paragraph styles so every heading matches
  • Set up columns and a masthead
  • Keep a multi-page document consistent
Desktop Publishing · Week 9 · Idea 1

Understand it

When a document has many pages, consistency matters more than any one page.

  • Styles: define Heading, Subheading, Body and Caption once (Google Docs: Format → Paragraph styles; Scribus: Edit → Styles). Change the style and every heading updates.
  • Master pages (Scribus, LibreOffice) or templates hold what repeats: margins, columns, page numbers, the footer.
  • Masthead: the newsletter's name and issue date across the top of page one.
  • Columns: two or three narrow columns read faster than one wide one.
  • Continue lines: "continued on page 3" when a story jumps.

Desktop Publishing · Week 9 · Key words

Key words

Paragraph style
a saved set of type settings applied to text
Master page
a background page holding what repeats
Masthead
the title block of a newsletter
Desktop Publishing · Week 9 · Practice

Now you do it

  1. Design a masthead for a Club newsletter
  2. Set up two-column pages with heading and body styles
  3. Add headers, footers and page numbers

Need a hand? Use Google Docs with a two-column section and three styles only.

Done early? Set up a master page in Scribus with columns and automatic page numbers.

Desktop Publishing · Week 9 · Assessment

How you will be assessed

  • You need to change the font of every heading in a 12-page newsletter. What is the fastest reliable way?
  • Show two pages of your newsletter with a masthead, two columns, consistent styles and page numbers.

Your work is marked against the rubric, and you may be asked to explain your choices. Show your own thinking.
